title: Approval impact table misreports rm targets whose paths contain whitespace or newlines (an existing file is shown as nonexistent)
description: For a gated exec the "system-computed impact" table is produced by SandboxManager._expand / _walk and preview_command. _expand hands the already-unquoted rm operand to sh as $1 and iterates over $1 unquoted, so the operand is word-split on IFS and each fragment is pathname-expanded before the [ -e ] existence test; results are newline-framed and re-split in Python, and _walk frames find output the same way. preview_command turns an empty match list into "삭제 시도 (현재 존재하지 않음)" and every returned line into a "삭제" row. The rm itself later runs through bash -c with the original quoting, so the computed path set and the executed path set differ: an agent whose workspace target contains a space obtains approval for a deletion the card describes as an apparent no-op, or for a card that lists unrelated decoy files, while the real file is deleted. Reproduced with the verbatim scripts: the card for a lone rm of an existing "final report.docx" showed exactly one row, "삭제 시도 (현재 존재하지 않음)", and no note.
root_cause: The preview path transport is not a lossless representation of a filesystem path. sandbox.py:559 iterates $1 unquoted under the default IFS, so an operand that shlex already unquoted (preview.py:33-44) is re-split into words and each word is expanded again before the existence test; matches are framed with printf "%s\n" and re-split by splitlines() (sandbox.py:562), and _walk's find | head output is split the same way (sandbox.py:565-569). preview.py:90-91 maps an empty expansion to the "does not currently exist" row and preview.py:96-98 maps each returned line to a deletion row, so a split operand both hides the real target and can manufacture paths the command will never touch. The executed command keeps its quoting (sandbox.py:411), so the card and the effect diverge.
intended_behavior: The affected list shown beside the approval must name exactly the paths the stored command will act on, so approving the card is equivalent to approving the effect: a path that exists must never be reported as nonexistent, and a path must never be listed as deleted unless the command deletes it.

trace.description: The agent posts tool=exec with body.args.command under its own sandbox token.
For a REQUIRE_APPROVAL decision (default_policy.yaml:12-16 routes rm to require_approval) the preview is computed while the approval is created, before any human sees it.
exec previews delegate to SandboxManager.preview with the raw command string.
preview_command runs with expand=_expand and walk=_walk bound to the running container.
Each rm operand (quotes already consumed by _split_segments, preview.py:33-44) is expanded once through the container callback.
The operand is passed as $1 and iterated unquoted, so the shell word-splits it on IFS and globs the fragments before [ -e "$p" ]; the surviving words are what get tested.
Matches are framed one per line and re-split with splitlines(), so a name containing a newline arrives as two or more fake paths.
An empty expansion becomes the "삭제 시도 (현재 존재하지 않음)" row and each returned line becomes a deletion row; the result is stored with the approval and rendered as the system-computed impact.

After the human approves, decide() snapshots (service.py:412) and _run_tool passes the stored command unchanged (service.py:126) to exec, which runs it verbatim through bash -c; the quoting is intact there, so the file the table called nonexistent is actually deleted.

evidence.description: for p in $1 - the operand is expanded without quotes under the default IFS, so a space splits it and each fragment is globbed; reproduced with only the cd target retargeted.
An empty match list becomes the "삭제 시도 (현재 존재하지 않음)" row - the false no-op statement for an existing but split path, produced with notes=[].
Matched paths become "삭제" rows, so split words (decoy names that exist) are presented as the deletion set.
out.splitlines() turns one filename containing a newline into several rows; expand("*") over fixtures "a\nb" and ok.txt returned [a, b, ok.txt].
_walk frames find output line by line (splitlines at 569), so a recursive rm over "dir with space/inner\nname.txt" reports "dir with space/inner" and "name.txt" instead of the real path.
The approved command runs as a single bash -c argument, so shell quoting is honoured and the computed set diverges from the executed set.
decide() snapshots before execution, which bounds the impact to low.
The per-segment note added for run-3 v17 shows the module already treats "the table may be incomplete" as security-relevant; the split-path case produces no note at all.

The table renders the not-existing row without the deletion highlight (only effect == 삭제 gets class del), so the sole row on the card looks like a failed no-op; the raw command is shown above it at line 8.
Control characters are escaped for display, so the defect is in the computed path set, not in the rendering.

conditions.description: A sandbox agent token (or prompt-injected code running as uid 1000 inside that sandbox) submits the rm; the default policy routes rm to require_approval, so the approval card is the only control between it and the deletion.
A human opens the pending approval in the /ui/approvals card or agentbox approve and presses approve, relying on the system-computed impact table rather than re-reading the raw command.

The rm operand names an existing /workspace path containing whitespace (space or tab) or a newline; the agent can produce that state itself, since creating a new file with write_file needs no approval.
Stock default_policy.yaml, where exec commands containing rm route to require_approval (default_policy.yaml:12-16).

execution.attacker_perspective: The sandbox agent wants to delete /workspace/final report.docx but wants the card not to say so, so it submits exec rm "final report.docx". The card describes the target as "삭제 시도 (현재 존재하지 않음)" - an apparently already-failed no-op - and with decoy names present it lists files that will not be touched, while the approved command deletes the real file.
payloads: decoy fixtures final and report.docx in the same directory
rm over a workspace containing a file named "a\nb"
rm notes.txt; mv important /tmp/important (run-3 v17 revalidation)
instructions: Create fixtures in the approved sandbox (tools/sbx.py v06, no network, read-only /target, writes only /scratch): a directory holding one file literally named final report.docx plus notes.txt.

Copy the sandbox.py:559 and sandbox.py:565 scripts verbatim, changing only cd /workspace to the fixture directory (the sandbox has no /workspace and uid 65534 cannot create one), and wrap them exactly as sandbox.py:560-562 / 567-569 do (decode, splitlines) to build the expand and walk callbacks.
Import agentbox.preview from /target (PYTHONPATH) and call preview_command('rm "final report.docx"', 200, expand, walk); compare the affected rows and notes with os.path.exists on the real file.
Repeat with decoy files final and report.docx present, and with fixtures named "a\nb" and "a\tb.txt" for the expand path and "dir with space/inner\nname.txt" for the walk path.
Re-run the run-3 v17 case rm notes.txt; mv important /tmp/important and check that its per-segment note still appears.
Show the sink: run sh -c 'rm "final report.docx"' in the fixture directory (the quoting sandbox.py:411 hands to bash) and confirm the file the table called nonexistent is gone.
execution.observed_result:
Case B: affected=[{path: "final report.docx", effect: "삭제 시도 (현재 존재하지 않음)"}], notes=[], real target exists: true. Case C (decoys present): affected=[{path: "final", effect: "삭제"}, {path: "report.docx", effect: "삭제"}] while the real target still exists and is never listed. Newline case: expand("*") -> ["a", "b", "ok.txt"] for files "a
b" and ok.txt, and the old find framing returned ["dir with space", "dir with space/inner", "name.txt"]. Sink: sh -c 'rm "final report.docx"' exited 0 and the directory went from [final report.docx, notes.txt] to [notes.txt]. Case A (revalidation): "rm notes.txt; mv important /tmp/important" produced the rm row AND the per-segment note, so the run-3 omission defect is fixed. The proposed fix was also executed against the same fixtures: with IFS= and NUL framing expand returned ["final report.docx"] and a single "a
b", and find -print0 | head -z kept "dir with space/inner
name.txt" whole. Everything ran inside tools/sbx.py v06.

remediation.strategy: Make both preview transports lossless. In _expand, disable IFS word splitting (IFS=) so the operand is tested as one word while pathname expansion still happens, and frame results with NUL instead of newline; in _walk, use find -print0 with head -z and split on NUL. Then one match is one path: the "does not currently exist" row is emitted only when the path really is absent, and no row names a path the command will not touch. Add a regression test that pushes names containing a space, a tab and a newline through both the non-recursive and the recursive branch and asserts the returned list equals the fixture paths.

code_changes.fixed_code:
def _expand(self, c, pattern: str) -> list[str]:
    """컨테이너 안에서 glob만 펼친다. 명령 치환은 일어나지 않는다."""
    script = ('cd /workspace; IFS=; for p in $1; do if [ -e "$p" ] || [ -L "$p" ]; then printf "%s\\0" "$p"; fi; done')
    res = c.exec_run(["sh", "-c", script, "_", pattern], user=AGENT_UID, demux=True)
    out = (res.output[0] or b"").decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    return [p for p in out.split("\0") if p]

def _walk(self, c, path: str, limit: int) -> list[str]:
    res = c.exec_run(["sh", "-c", 'cd /workspace; case "$1" in -*) set -- "./$1" "$2";; esac; find "$1" -print0 2>/dev/null | head -z -n "$2"',
                      "_", path, str(limit)],
                     user=AGENT_UID, demux=True)
    out = (res.output[0] or b"").decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    return [p for p in out.split("\0") if p]

likelihood.reason: The mechanics are deterministic for any rm operand naming a /workspace path with whitespace or a newline, and the agent can create such a name itself with an ungated write_file before requesting the rm, so the condition is attacker-chosen rather than accidental; exploitation still needs the approver to rely on the table instead of the raw command displayed immediately above it, and only rm and curl reach this preview.

impact.reason: What is lost is informed consent on the card, not a boundary: the effect is a deletion inside the requesting agent's own /workspace, the resource class the rm approval governs, decide() snapshots immediately before execution so the files are recoverable, and the decoy rows are misleading text rather than an additional capability.

confidence.reason: Every cited line was re-read in 9805d91, the divergence was reproduced inside the approved sandbox with the verbatim _expand/_walk scripts (only the cd target substituted) and the verbatim preview_command, the sink step confirms the stored command keeps its quoting and really deletes the file, and the proposed fix was executed against the same fixtures.
